<p>This page documents all REST API endpoints exposed by the FastAPI backend. These endpoints provide access to live TV streams, decryption keys, content proxying, playlist generation, and logo serving. For information about the background channel update task, see <a href="/gookie-dev/StepDaddyLiveHD/5.2-background-tasks" class="text-neutral-300 hover:text-neutral-200 hover:underline">Background Tasks</a>. For details on the logo caching implementation, see <a href="/gookie-dev/StepDaddyLiveHD/5.3-logo-caching" class="text-neutral-300 hover:text-neutral-200 hover:underline">Logo Caching</a>.</p>

</ul>

For in-depth technical details about specific components, see [Architecture](#3) and subsequent sections.\n\n## Purpose and Scope\n\nStepDaddyLiveHD is a self-hosted IPTV proxy system that enables users to stream over 1,000 live TV channels through a web interface or external IPTV clients. The system acts as an intermediary between end users and the dlhd.dad content provider, handling authentication, stream resolution, and content delivery.\n\nThe application is built entirely in Python using the Reflex full-stack framework, which combines a React-based frontend with a FastAPI backend. StepDaddyLiveHD\n\nStepDaddyLiveHD is an IPTV aggregation and proxy service that:\n\n1. **Discovers Channels**: Scrapes and indexes live TV channels from dlhd.dad\n2. **Resolves Streams**: Performs multi-step authentication to obtain working M3U8 playlists\n3. **Proxies Content**: Routes all stream requests through the local server with encrypted URLs\n4. **Provides UI**: Offers a web-based channel browser with search and filtering capabilities\n5. **Supports IPTV Clients**: Generates M3U8 playlists compatible with VLC, Jellyfin, and other media players\n\nThe system maintains a metadata When TLS is used, the API_URL \n# is assumed to be the same as the frontend.\nARG API_URL\n\n# It uses a reverse proxy to serve the frontend statically and proxy \n# to backend from a single exposed Internet[\"Internet\"]\n        LoadBalancer[\"Load Balancer\u003cbr/\u003eTLS Termination\u003cbr/\u003eSSL Certificate\"]\n        Container1[\"Container Instance 1\u003cbr/\u003eHTTP :3000\"]\n `PROXY_CONTENT` environment variable controls whether video content is proxied through the application server [.env:3]():\n\n```bash\nPROXY_CONTENT=\"TRUE\"  # Proxy video segments through requests\u003cbr/\u003e- Less control over access |\n\n**Recommendation**: Use `PROXY_CONTENT=FALSE` in production for better performance unless you need strict access control or request variable [.env:4]():\n\n```bash\n# No proxy\nSOCKS5=\"\"\n\n# Authenticated SOCKS5 proxy\nSOCKS5=\"user:password@proxy.example.com:1080\"\n```\n\nThis proxy is used for all requests to the dlhd.dad service, including channel list fetching and stream resolution. It does not affect CDN video content requests.\n\n**Sources**: [.env:4](), [README.md:69]()\n\n### Container Resource Management\n\nThe container runs three services concurrently:\n\n| Service | Process Type | Resource Usage |\n|---------|--------------|----------------|\n| Caddy | Background daemon | Low CPU, Low memory |\n| Redis | Background daemon | Low CPU, Medium memory (depends on cache) |\n| Reflex Backend | Foreground process | Medium CPU, Medium memory |\n\n**Recommended Resource Limits**:\n\n```yaml\n# docker-compose.yml\nservices:\n  step-daddy-live-hd:\n    deploy:\n      resources:\n        limits:\n          cpus: '2'\n          memory: 1G\n        reservations:\n          cpus: '0.5'\n          memory: 512M\n```\n\n**Sources**: [Dockerfile:54-56]()\n\n### Signal Handling\n\nThe container uses `SIGKILL` as the stop signal [Dockerfile:49]():\n\n```dockerfile\n# Needed until Reflex properly passes SIGTERM on backend.\nSTOPSIGNAL SIGKILL\n```\n\nThis is a workaround for Reflex's signal handling behavior. The container stops immediately without graceful shutdown. Be aware that:\n- In-flight requests may be terminated\n- Background tasks may not complete\n- Redis data is not persisted (in-memory only)\n\nFor production, consider implementing health checks and ensuring clients can retry failed requests.\n\n**Sources**: [Dockerfile:48-49]()\n\n### Restart Policy\n\nThe docker-compose configuration includes an automatic restart policy [docker-compose.yml:18]():\n\n```yaml\nrestart: unless-stopped\n```\n\nThis ensures the container automatically restarts on failure or host reboot, improving service availability.\n\n**Sources**: [docker-compose.yml:18]()\n\n### Redis Persistence\n\nThe Redis server starts without persistence configuration [Dockerfile:55]():\n\n```bash\nredis-server --daemonize yes\n```\n\n**Implications**:\n- All cached data is lost on container restart\n- Channel list and metadata are regenerated on startup\n- Logo cache is stored in filesystem, not Redis\n- No Redis RDB/AOF files are created\n\nFor production deployments requiring persistent cache across restarts, consider mounting a volume for Redis data or using an external Redis instance.\n\n**Sources**: [Dockerfile:55]()\n\n### Monitoring and Logging\n\nThe container is configured with unbuffered Python output [Dockerfile:42]():\n\n```dockerfile\nENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1\n```\n\nThis ensures logs are immediately visible via `docker [Caddyfile](Caddyfile)\n- [Dockerfile](Dockerfile)\n\n\u003c/details\u003e\n\n\n\n## Purpose and Scope\n\nThis document describes the Caddy reverse proxy configuration that serves as the routing layer for StepDaddyLiveHD. Caddy handles all incoming HTTP requests on the exposed port, routing API calls to the FastAPI backend (running on port 8000) and serving static frontend files from `/srv`. This configuration enables the system to expose a single port while maintaining separation between frontend and backend components.\n\nFor information about the Docker container architecture and service startup sequence, see [Docker Architecture](#9.1). For production deployment considerations including TLS termination, see [Production Considerations](#9.3).\n\n**Sources:** [Dockerfile:1-56](), [Caddyfile:1-17]()\n\n---\n\n## Configuration File Structure\n\nThe reverse proxy is configured via the `Caddyfile` located at the repository root. This file defines how Caddy routes requests between the static frontend and the dynamic backend API.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    Caddyfile[\"Caddyfile\"]\n    Port[\"Port Binding\u003cbr/\u003e:{$PORT}\"]\n    Encoding[\"Compression\u003cbr/\u003eencode gzip\"]\n    BackendMatcher[\"@backend_routes matcher\u003cbr/\u003epath /_event/* /ping /_upload*\u003cbr/\u003e/stream/* /key/* /content/*\u003cbr/\u003e/playlist.m3u8 /logo/*\"]\n    BackendHandler[\"handle @backend_routes\u003cbr/\u003ereverse_proxy localhost:8000\"]\n    StaticHandler[\"handle (default)\u003cbr/\u003eroot * /srv\u003cbr/\u003etry_files + file_server\"]\n    \n    Caddyfile --\u003e Port\n    Caddyfile --\u003e Encoding\n    Caddyfile --\u003e BackendMatcher\n    Caddyfile --\u003e StaticHandler\n    \n    BackendMatcher --\u003e BackendHandler\n    \n    Port -.-\u003e |\"Set from $PORT env var\"| ENV[\"Environment Variable\"]\n    BackendHandler -.-\u003e |\"Proxy to\"| FastAPI[\"FastAPI Backend\u003cbr/\u003elocalhost:8000\"]\n    StaticHandler -.-\u003e |\"Serve from\"| SRV[\"/srv directory\u003cbr/\u003eCompiled frontend\"]\n```\n\n**Sources:** [Caddyfile:1-17]()\n\n---\n\n## Port Binding and Environment Variables\n\nCaddy binds to the port specified by the `$PORT` environment variable, which is configured during container build and runtime.\n\n| Configuration Stage | File | Line Reference | Default Value |\n|---------------------|------|----------------|---------------|\n| Build Argument | `Dockerfile` | [Dockerfile:1]() | `3000` |\n| Runtime Environment | `Dockerfile` | [Dockerfile:42]() | Inherits from ARG `$PORT` |\n| Caddyfile Binding | `Caddyfile` | [Caddyfile:1]() | `:{$PORT}` |\n\nThe syntax `:{$PORT}` in the Caddyfile creates a site block that listens on all interfaces on the specified port. This is formatted as `:PORT` without an explicit hostname, which makes Caddy respond to all host headers.\n\n**Sources:** [Caddyfile:1](), [Dockerfile:1](), [Dockerfile:42]()\n\n---\n\n## Request Routing Logic\n\nCaddy uses a matcher-based routing system to distinguish between backend API requests and static frontend requests. The routing flow follows this decision tree:\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    Request[\"Incoming HTTP Request\u003cbr/\u003ePort {$PORT}\"]\n    Gzip[\"encode gzip\u003cbr/\u003eApply compression\"]\n    Matcher{\"@backend_routes matcher\u003cbr/\u003eDoes path match?\"}\n    \n    BackendPaths[\"Backend Path Patterns:\u003cbr/\u003e/_event/*\u003cbr/\u003e/ping\u003cbr/\u003e/_upload, /_upload/*\u003cbr/\u003e/stream/*\u003cbr/\u003e/key/*\u003cbr/\u003e/content/*\u003cbr/\u003e/playlist.m3u8\u003cbr/\u003e/logo/*\"]\n    \n    ReverseProxy[\"reverse_proxy localhost:8000\u003cbr/\u003eForward to FastAPI\"]\n    \n    StaticRoot[\"root * /srv\u003cbr/\u003eSet document root\"]\n    TryFiles[\"try_files {path} {path}/ /404.html\u003cbr/\u003eAttempt to locate file\"]\n    FileServer[\"file_server\u003cbr/\u003eServe static content\"]\n    \n    FastAPI[\"FastAPI Backend\u003cbr/\u003elocalhost:8000\"]\n    Client[\"Response to Client\"]\n    \n    Request --\u003e Gzip\n    Gzip --\u003e Matcher\n    \n    Matcher --\u003e|\"Yes\"| ReverseProxy\n    Matcher --\u003e|\"No\"| StaticRoot\n    \n    BackendPaths -.-\u003e|\"Defines\"| Matcher\n    \n    ReverseProxy --\u003e FastAPI\n    FastAPI --\u003e Client\n    \n    StaticRoot --\u003e TryFiles\n    TryFiles --\u003e FileServer\n    FileServer --\u003e Client\n```\n\n**Sources:** [Caddyfile:1-17]()\n\n---\n\n## Backend Route Matching\n\nThe `@backend_routes` named matcher identifies requests that should be proxied to the FastAPI backend. This matcher is defined using the `path` directive with multiple patterns:\n\n```caddyfile\n@backend_routes path /_event/* /ping /_upload /_upload/* /stream/* /key/* /content/* /playlist.m3u8 /logo/*\n```\n\n### Backend Route Patterns\n\n| Route Pattern | Purpose | Backend Handler |\n|---------------|---------|-----------------|\n| `/_event/*` | Reflex event WebSocket and SSE connections | Reflex backend event system |\n| `/ping` | Health check endpoint | Reflex backend |\n| `/_upload`, `/_upload/*` | File upload endpoints | Reflex backend upload handler |\n| `/stream/*` | M3U8 playlist generation | `backend.stream_endpoint()` |\n| `/key/*` | Decryption key proxying | `backend.key_endpoint()` |\n| `/content/*` | Video segment proxying | `backend.content_endpoint()` |\n| `/playlist.m3u8` | Full M3U8 playlist download | `backend.playlist_endpoint()` |\n| `/logo/*` | Logo image proxying | `backend.logo_endpoint()` |\n\nThe patterns prefixed with `/_` are Reflex framework internals, while the content delivery patterns (`/stream/*`, `/key/*`, `/content/*`, `/logo/*`) correspond to custom API endpoints defined in the backend module. For detailed API endpoint documentation, see [API Endpoints](#5.1).\n\n**Sources:** [Caddyfile:5-8]()\n\n---\n\n## Reverse Proxy Handler\n\nWhen a request matches `@backend_routes`, Caddy forwards it to the FastAPI backend using the `reverse_proxy` directive:\n\n```caddyfile\nhandle @backend_routes {\n    reverse_proxy localhost:8000\n}\n```\n\nThis configuration establishes a proxy connection to `localhost:8000`, where the Reflex backend server is listening. The proxy maintains the original request path, headers, and body, forwarding them transparently to the backend.\n\n### Backend Server Location\n\nThe FastAPI backend is started by the Reflex framework in backend-only mode on port 8000:\n\n```bash\nreflex run --env prod --backend-only\n```\n\nThis command is executed in the container startup sequence defined at [Dockerfile:56](). The backend binds to `localhost:8000` by default, which is only accessible within the container. External access is exclusively through the Caddy reverse proxy on the exposed `$PORT`.\n\n**Sources:** [Caddyfile:6-8](), [Dockerfile:56]()\n\n---\n\n## Static File Serving\n\nRequests that do not match `@backend_routes` are handled by the default handler, which serves static files from the `/srv` directory:\n\n```caddyfile\nhandle {\n    root * /srv\n    route {\n        try_files {path} {path}/ /404.html\n        file_server\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Static File Serving Process\n\n```mermaid\nsequenceDiagram\n    participant Client\n    participant Caddy\n    participant SRV as \"/srv filesystem\"\n    \n    Client-\u003e\u003eCaddy: GET /index.html\n    \n    rect rgb(240, 240, 240)\n        Note over Caddy,SRV: Static File Resolution\n        Caddy-\u003e\u003eSRV: Check /srv/index.html\n        alt File exists\n            SRV--\u003e\u003eCaddy: File found\n            Caddy-\u003e\u003eClient: 200 OK + file content\n        else File not found\n Resolution Strategy\n\nThe `try_files` directive implements a fallback chain:\n\n1. **Exact path match**: Attempts to serve the file at the exact requested path (e.g., `/about.html` → serves `/srv/404.html` with a 404 status code\n\nThis strategy supports both traditional multi-page applications and single-page applications with client-side routing.\n\n**Sources:** [Caddyfile:10-16]()\n\n---\n\n## Static Content Location\n\nThe static frontend files are compiled during the Docker build process and placed in `/srv`:\n\n```dockerfile\nRUN REFLEX_API_URL=${API_URL:-http://localhost:$PORT} reflex export --loglevel debug --frontend-only --no-zip \u0026\u0026 mv .web/build/client/* /srv/ \u0026\u0026 rm -rf .web\n```\n\nThis build step:\n1. Exports the Reflex frontend as static files to `.web/build/client/`\n2. Moves all compiled assets to `/srv/`\n3. Removes the temporary `.web` directory\n\nThe `/srv` directory contains:\n- HTML files (`index.html`, `404.html`, etc.)\n- JavaScript bundles\n- CSS stylesheets\n- Static assets (images, fonts)\n- Reflex-generated React components\n\n**Sources:** [Dockerfile:32](), [Dockerfile:46]()\n\n---\n\n## Compression Configuration\n\nCaddy applies gzip compression to all responses using the `encode` directive:\n\n```caddyfile\nencode gzip\n```\n\nThis directive is placed at the site block level, meaning it applies to all requests before any handler logic executes. Caddy automatically:\n\n- Compresses responses with content types that benefit from compression (text/html, text/css, application/javascript, etc.)\n- Sets the `Content-Encoding: gzip` header\n- Handles the `Accept-Encoding` negotiation with clients\n- Skips compression for already-compressed formats (images, videos)\n\nCompression reduces bandwidth usage significantly for text-based assets, which is particularly important for the frontend JavaScript bundles and API responses containing channel metadata.\n\n**Sources:** [Caddyfile:3]()\n\n---\n\n## Startup and Service Orchestration\n\nCaddy is started as part of the container initialization sequence before the backend server:\n\n```bash\ncaddy start \u0026\u0026 \\\n    redis-server --daemonize yes \u0026\u0026 \\\n    exec reflex run --env prod --backend-only\n```\n\n### Startup Sequence\n\n1. **Caddy starts** in background mode (`caddy start`)\n2. **Redis starts** as a daemon (`redis-server --daemonize yes`)\n3. **Reflex backend starts** in foreground mode (`exec reflex run --backend-only`)\n\nCaddy's `start` command runs it as a background service that continues running independently. This allows the container's main process to be the Reflex backend, which handles graceful shutdown signals. **Backend:** Runs on port 8000 with auto-restart on file changes\n- **File Watching:** Monitors `.py` and `.jsx` files for changes\n- **Reload Behavior:** \n  - Python changes → Backend restarts automatically\n  - React component changes → Frontend hot reloads without page refresh\n  - State class changes → Full page reload required\n- **Build Time:** Faster incremental builds\n- **Bundle Size:** Larger, includes development tools and source maps\n\n### Production Mode (`reflex run --env prod`)\n\nWhen running in production mode:\n\n- **Frontend:** Precompiled static assets served directly\n- **Backend:** Runs on port 8000 without auto-restart\n- **File Watching:** Disabled\n- **Reload Behavior:** Manual restart required for any changes\n- **Build Time:** Slower initial build, optimized for performance\n- **Bundle Size:** Smaller, minified and tree-shaken\n\n**Best Practice:** Always develop in development mode and test in production mode before deployment.\n\n---\n\n## Running the Development Server\n\n### Basic Development Server\n\n```bash\nreflex run\n```\n\nThis starts both frontend and backend servers:\n\n```\n────────────────────────────────────────────\nStarting Reflex App\n────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nBackend running at: http://localhost:8000\nFrontend running at: http://localhost:3000\n```\n\nThe application is accessible at `http://localhost:3000`.\n\n### Custom Port\n\nTo run on a different port:\n\n```bash\nreflex run --frontend-port 8080 --backend-port 8001\n```\n\n### Backend Only (API Development)\n\nTo run only the backend API server:\n\n```bash\nreflex run --backend-only\n```\n\nThis is useful when:\n- Developing API endpoints in [backend.py]()\n- Testing the StepDaddy core module\n- Frontend is already compiled and served separately\n\n### Frontend Only (UI Development)\n\nTo run only the frontend development server:\n\n```bash\nreflex run --frontend-only\n```\n\nThis requires a separately running backend instance.\n\n**Sources:** [README.md:56-59]()\n\n---\n\n## Development Workflow\n\nThe following diagram shows the typical development cycle and how changes propagate through the system:\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TB\n    subgraph \"Developer Actions\"\n        EditPy[\"Edit Python Files\u003cbr/\u003e*.py in StepDaddyLiveHD/\"]\n        EditJSX[\"Edit JSX Files\u003cbr/\u003eassets/player.jsx\"]\n        EditState[\"Edit State Class\u003cbr/\u003eStepDaddyLiveHD.py\"]\n    end\n    \n    subgraph \"File Watcher\"\n        Watch[\"reflex run\u003cbr/\u003eFile Monitoring\"]\n    end\n    \n    subgraph \"Reload Mechanisms\"\n        BackendRestart[\"Backend Restart\u003cbr/\u003eFastAPI reloads\"]\n        FrontendHMR[\"Frontend HMR\u003cbr/\u003eReact Hot Reload\"]\n        FullReload[\"Full Page Reload\u003cbr/\u003eState changes\"]\n    end\n    \n    subgraph \"Testing\"\n        Browser[\"Browser Refresh\u003cbr/\u003elocalhost:3000\"]\n        API[\"API Testing\u003cbr/\u003ecurl/httpx\"]\n        Console[\"Check Logs\u003cbr/\u003eTerminal Output\"]\n    end\n    \n    EditPy --\u003e Watch\n    EditJSX --\u003e Watch\n    EditState --\u003e Watch\n    \n    Watch --\u003e|Python change| BackendRestart\n    Watch --\u003e|JSX change| FrontendHMR\n    Watch --\u003e|State change| FullReload\n    \n    BackendRestart --\u003e Browser\n    FrontendHMR --\u003e Browser\n    FullReload --\u003e Browser\n    \n    Browser --\u003e Console\n    API --\u003e Console\n```\n\n**Sources:** [README.md:56-59](), [rxconfig.py:1-20]()\n\n### Common Development Tasks\n\n#### 1. Adding a New API Endpoint\n\n1. Edit [StepDaddyLiveHD/backend.py]()\n2. Save the file\n3. Backend automatically restarts\n4. Test endpoint at `http://localhost:8000/your-endpoint`\n\n#### 2. Modifying UI Components\n\n1. Edit files in [StepDaddyLiveHD/components/]() or [StepDaddyLiveHD/pages/]()\n2. Save the file\n3. Frontend automatically updates via HMR\n4. View changes at `http://localhost:3000`\n\n#### 3. Updating State Logic\n\n1. Edit `State` class in [StepDaddyLiveHD/StepDaddyLiveHD.py]()\n2. Save the file\n3. Both frontend and backend reload\n4. Browser page refreshes automatically\n\n#### 4. Testing Stream Resolution\n\n1. Edit [StepDaddyLiveHD/step_daddy.py]()\n2. Backend restarts\n3. Test via watch page or direct API call:\n   ```bash\n   curl http://localhost:8000/stream/123.m3u8\n   ```\n\n---\n\n## Environment Configuration for Development\n\n### Configuration File\n\nThe [rxconfig.py:1-20]() file controls application configuration. It reads environment variables and configures Reflex:\n\n```python\nimport os\n\nproxy_content = os.environ.get(\"PROXY_CONTENT\", \"TRUE\").upper() == \"TRUE\"\nsocks5 = os.environ.get(\"SOCKS5\", \"\")\n```\n\n**Sources:** [rxconfig.py:5-6]()\n\n### Development Environment Variables\n\nCreate a `.env` file in the project root for local development configuration:\n\n```bash\n# Server Configuration\nPORT=3000\nAPI_URL=http://localhost:3000\n\n# Feature Flags\nPROXY_CONTENT=TRUE\n\n# Optional: SOCKS5 Proxy\nSOCKS5=\n\n# Development Mode\nENV=dev\n```\n\n### Environment Variable Reference\n\n| Variable | Default | Purpose | Development Recommendation |\n|----------|---------|---------|---------------------------|\n| `PORT` | 3000 | Frontend server port | Keep as 3000 for consistency |\n| `API_URL` | `http://localhost:3000` | Base URL for API requests | Use `http://localhost:3000` |\n| `PROXY_CONTENT` | `TRUE` | Proxy video segments through backend | Keep `TRUE` for testing full flow |\n| `SOCKS5` | (empty) | SOCKS5 proxy for dlhd.dad requests | Leave empty unless testing proxy |\n\n**Sources:** [rxconfig.py:5-6](), [README.md:63-77]()\n\n### Loading Environment Variables\n\nTo use the `.env` file, export variables before running:\n\n**Linux/macOS:**\n```bash\nexport $(cat .env | xargs)\nreflex run\n```\n\n**Windows PowerShell:**\n```powershell\nGet-Content .env | ForEach-Object {\n    $name, $value = $_.split('=')\n    Set-Content env:\\$name $value\n}\nreflex run\n```\n\n### Configuration Access in Code\n\nThe configuration is accessed via the `rx.Config` object:\n\n```python\nimport reflex as rx\n\n# Access configuration\nconfig = rx.config\nproxy_content = config.proxy_content\nsocks5 = config.socks5\n```\n\n**Sources:** [rxconfig.py:10-19]()\n\n---\n\n## Local Redis Setup (Optional)\n\nWhile Redis is required in production, development mode works without it:\n\n```mermaid\ngraph LR\n    subgraph \"Development (Optional Redis)\"\n        DevApp[\"reflex run\"]\n        DevRedis[\"Redis\u003cbr/\u003eOptional\u003cbr/\u003eFor testing caching\"]\n        DevMemory[\"In-Memory Fallback\u003cbr/\u003eNo persistence\"]\n    end\n    \n    subgraph \"Production (Required Redis)\"\n        ProdApp[\"Backend Server\"]\n        ProdRedis[\"Redis\u003cbr/\u003eRequired\u003cbr/\u003eLogo caching\"]\n    end\n    \n    DevApp -.-\u003e|Optional| DevRedis\n    DevApp --\u003e|Fallback| DevMemory\n    ProdApp --\u003e|Required| ProdRedis\n```\n\n### Installing Redis Locally\n\n**Linux:**\n```bash\nsudo apt-get install redis-server\nredis-server --daemonize yes\n```\n\n**macOS:**\n```bash\nbrew install redis\nbrew services start redis\n```\n\n**Windows:**\nUse Docker or WSL2 with Linux instructions.\n\n### Verifying Redis Connection\n\n```bash\nredis-cli ping\n# Expected output: PONG\n```\n\nThe application will automatically detect and use Redis if running on `localhost:6379`.\n\n**Sources:** Based on architecture documentation showing Redis usage for caching\n\n---\n\n## IDE and Editor Setup\n\n### Recommended IDE: VS Code\n\nInstall the following extensions:\n\n| Extension | Purpose |\n|-----------|---------|\n| Python | Python language support and IntelliSense |\n| Pylance | Fast Python type checking |\n| Reflex | Syntax highlighting for Reflex components |\n| ESLint | JavaScript/JSX linting |\n| Tailwind CSS IntelliSense | CSS class autocompletion |\n\n### VS Code Workspace Settings\n\nCreate `.vscode/settings.json`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"python.defaultInterpreterPath\": \"${workspaceFolder}/venv/bin/python\",\n  \"python.linting.enabled\": true,\n  \"python.linting.pylintEnabled\": false,\n  \"python.linting.flake8Enabled\": true,\n  \"python.formatting.provider\": \"black\",\n  \"editor.formatOnSave\": true,\n  \"[python]\": {\n    \"editor.defaultFormatter\": \"ms-python.black-formatter\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Project Structure in IDE\n\n```\nStepDaddyLiveHD/\n├── StepDaddyLiveHD/          # Main application package\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── StepDaddyLiveHD.py    # Main app + State\n│   ├── backend.py            # FastAPI endpoints\n│   ├── step_daddy.py         # Core stream resolution\n│   ├── utils.py              # Encryption utilities\n│   ├── pages/                # Page components\n│   ├── components/           # Reusable UI components\n│   └── meta.json             # Channel metadata\n├── assets/                   # Static assets\n│   └── player.jsx            # Media player JSX\n├── .web/                     # Generated frontend (gitignored)\n├── venv/                     # Virtual environment (gitignored)\n├── requirements.txt          # Python dependencies\n├── rxconfig.py              # Reflex configuration\n└── README.md\n```\n\n**Sources:** Based on project structure analysis\n\n---\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Common Issues and Solutions\n\n#### Issue: `reflex: command not found`\n\n**Cause:** Virtual environment not activated or Reflex not installed.\n\n**Solution:**\n```bash\nsource venv/bin/activate\npip install -r requirements.txt\n```\n\n#### Issue: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'curl_cffi'`\n\n**Cause:** Dependencies not fully installed.\n\n**Solution:**\n```bash\npip install -r requirements.txt --force-reinstall\n```\n\n#### Issue: Frontend fails to start with \"Port 3000 already in use\"\n\n**Cause:** Another process is using port 3000.\n\n**Solution:**\n```bash\n# Find and kill the process\nlsof -ti:3000 | xargs kill -9\n\n# Or use a different port\nreflex run --frontend-port 8080\n```\n\n#### Issue: Backend changes not reflecting\n\n**Cause:** Hot reload failed or cached imports.\n\n**Solution:**\n```bash\n# Stop the server (Ctrl+C)\n# Clean generated files\nrm -rf .web/__pycache__\nrm -rf StepDaddyLiveHD/__pycache__\n\n# Restart\nreflex run\n```\n\n#### Issue: \"Failed to fetch channels\"\n\n**Cause:** Network connectivity or dlhd.dad is unreachable.\n\n**Solution:**\n```bash\n# Test direct connectivity\ncurl https://dlhd.dad\n\n# If blocked, configure SOCKS5 proxy\nexport SOCKS5=user:pass@proxy.example.com:1080\nreflex run\n```\n\n#### Issue: JSX changes not updating\n\n**Cause:** Frontend build cache.\n\n**Solution:**\n```bash\n# Clean frontend build\nrm -rf .web/public\nreflex run\n```\n\n### Debug Mode\n\nEnable verbose logging for troubleshooting:\n\n```bash\n# Set debug level\nexport REFLEX_DEBUG=True\nreflex run\n```\n\nThis provides detailed logs for:\n- HTTP requests and responses\n- State updates and event handlers\n- Component rendering cycles\n- Backend API calls\n\n**Sources:** Based on Reflex development best practices and common Python web development troubleshooting\n\n---\n\n## Development Server Architecture\n\nThis diagram shows how the development server components interact and how they differ from
